reviewStatusSummary.note: NO FIXTURE HAS BEEN REVIEWED BY A QUALIFIED HUMAN. Every case below is PROVISIONAL: the expected values are the assistant's reading of the stated grading contract, not teacher ground truth. Do not report agreement figures from this file as grading validity.

caseSchema.question: the item as generated (instructions, prompt, answerKey, acceptedAnswers, rubric, targetRule, maxMarks)
caseSchema.deterministic: true when the production grading path decides this case WITHOUT an AI call (the only cases CI may score)
caseSchema.provenance: who authored the expectation and when
caseSchema.rationale: why the expectation is what it is

question.targetRule: present simple: third person singular takes -s

question.instructions: Complete the sentence about a sequence of past events.
question.prompt: By 2019, the company ___ (open) five branches in Asia.

criteria: past perfect for a state completed before a past reference time

question.targetRule: past perfect for completion before a past reference point

cases.rationale: Grammatical in isolation but wrong for the reference-time relation the rubric demands. NOTE: the deterministic path cannot reason about context — it decides only because this response is not the key or a listed alternative, which is precisely why the objective path must not be used to judge free-form context.

question.instructions: Choose the sentence that follows the zero conditional pattern.
question.prompt: A) If it rains, we would stay home. B) If it rains, we stay home. C) If it rained, we stayed home. D) If it will rain, we stay home.
question.targetRule: zero conditional (if + present simple, present simple)

cases.rationale: Only B uses present simple in both clauses.

question.prompt: The coffee is ___ hot to drink. A) enough B) too C) too much D) much too

criteria: too + adjective before an infinitive of result

cases.rationale: 'too hot to drink' is the standard construction.

question.prompt: There are ___ chairs for everyone, so nobody has to stand. (enough / too)

criteria: enough before a plural noun expresses sufficiency

cases.rationale: 'chairs enough' would be ungrammatical; enough precedes the noun here.

question.prompt: There are ___ chairs for everyone, so nobody has to stand. (enough / too)

criteria: enough before a plural noun expresses sufficiency

cases.rationale: 'too chairs' is ungrammatical and contradicts the clause that follows.

question.prompt: He ___ (finish) the report.
question.targetRule: tense choice without a time reference

cases.rationale: Without a time reference several tenses are grammatical, so the generated item must list them as accepted alternatives; this case proves the contract is honoured when the author lists them.

question.instructions: Write one sentence using the zero conditional about a general truth.
question.prompt: Write about the effect of heat on ice.
question.answerKey: If you heat ice, it melts.
acceptedAnswers: If ice is heated, it melts.

cases.studentResponse: If I heat ice yesterday, it will melted.
cases.rationale: PROVISIONAL AI-graded case: wrong conditional form plus tense and morphology errors. Requires the provider and a human reviewer before its expectation can be treated as evidence.

question.instructions: Write one sentence using the zero conditional about a general truth.

question.answerKey: If you heat ice, it melts.
acceptedAnswers: If ice is heated, it melts.

cases.studentResponse: If you study hard, you pass exams.
cases.rationale: PROVISIONAL: form and general-truth semantics are correct but the sentence is off-topic, so the rubric's relevance criterion should cost a mark. The exact mark is a human judgement call.

question.prompt: She finished the report. Then the meeting started.
question.answerKey: She had finished the report before the meeting started.
acceptedAnswers: She had finished the report before the meeting began.
Before the meeting started, she had finished the report.

criteria: past perfect for the earlier action

cases.studentResponse: Before the meeting began, she had finished the report.
cases.rationale: PROVISIONAL: reordered clause with a synonym ('began') — the rubric explicitly accepts equivalent wording. Guards against exact-string grading.

question.instructions: Use 'too' in one sentence to describe an excess.
question.prompt: Write one sentence with too about the soup.
question.answerKey: The soup is too salty to eat.
acceptedAnswers: The soup was too salty to eat.

cases.rationale: PROVISIONAL: the target structure is absent (very ≠ too), so the mark is clear even though the sentence is grammatical.
